Import intervals from a BED file

Source: R/intervals-import.R
gintervals.import_bed.Rd

Reads a BED file, plain or gzipped, and returns a misha 1D intervals data frame. Track/browser/comment header lines are skipped automatically. Chromosome names are normalized through the active database's CHROM_ALIAS mechanism (so chr1 <-> 1 works without explicit configuration).

Usage

gintervals.import_bed(
  file = NULL,
  name = TRUE,
  score = TRUE,
  strand = TRUE,
  keep_order = FALSE,
  format = NULL
)

Arguments

file

path to a BED file (.bed or .bed.gz) or a bigBed file. Zip archives are not supported - unzip them first.

name

if TRUE and a 4th column exists, include it as name.

score

if TRUE and a 5th (numeric) column exists, include it as score.

strand

if TRUE and a 6th column exists, include it as strand (mapped to 1/-1/0).

keep_order

if TRUE, return the intervals in the file's order (header and comment lines skipped) instead of sorting them.

format

one of "bed", "narrowPeak" or "broadPeak". NULL guesses from the file name: a name ending in .narrowPeak or .narrowPeak.gz (any case) is narrowPeak, .broadPeak or .broadPeak.gz is broadPeak, anything else is BED.

Value

A 1D intervals data frame, sorted by chrom and start unless keep_order is TRUE.

Details

BED is already 0-based half-open, so coordinates are taken as-is.

A bigBed file (recognized by its first bytes, whatever its name) is read natively. Its columns are chrom, start, end and then its other fields in the file's order, named by the file's autoSql: fields of a numeric autoSql type (int, uint, short, ushort, byte, ubyte, float, double, bigint) are numeric, the others (string, lstring, char[n], enum, set, arrays) are kept as the text stored, and so is itemRgb (BED field 9, "R,G,B" text although autoSql declares it a uint). name, score and strand apply to the fields of those names. The fields of a bigBed without autoSql get the names UCSC's tools give them (name, score, strand, thickStart, thickEnd, reserved, blockCount, blockSizes, chromStarts, ...). As in gtrack.import of a bigWig, records on chromosomes the database lacks are skipped with a message (a warning if one of them looks like a primary chromosome), and records past the end of their chromosome are clipped to it (dropped if they start past it) with a warning. format must be NULL for a bigBed.

ENCODE narrowPeak (BED6+4) and broadPeak (BED6+3) files carry extra columns, which are added after the BED columns under their UCSC names: signalValue, pValue and qValue (numeric) for both, and peak (integer) for narrowPeak. peak is the summit's offset from start; -1 means no summit was called, and is kept as-is.

By default the intervals are sorted by chrom and start. With keep_order = TRUE they stay in the file's order, so row i is the i-th data line, as peak IDs that are row numbers expect. The functions below accept unsorted intervals. gextract, gscreen, gintervals.canonic and the set operations return their rows in genomic order (gextract's intervalID column gives the input row), while gseq.extract, gintervals.annotate, gintervals.normalize and gintervals.summary return one row per input row in input order. gintervals() sorts its input.

See also

gintervals.import_gff, gintervals.import_vcf.

Examples


gdb.init_examples()
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".narrowPeak")
writeLines(c(
    "chr1\t20000\t20400\tpeak_1\t500\t.\t8.1\t12.3\t10.2\t150",
    "chr1\t10000\t10300\tpeak_2\t800\t.\t9.4\t15.0\t12.8\t120"
), f)
peaks <- gintervals.import_bed(f, keep_order = TRUE)
peaks
#>   chrom start   end strand   name score signalValue pValue qValue peak
#> 1  chr1 20000 20400      0 peak_1   500         8.1   12.3   10.2  150
#> 2  chr1 10000 10300      0 peak_2   800         9.4   15.0   12.8  120

# 200 bp windows centred on the summits, in the file's order: the summit
# is at (start + end) %/% 2. Drop rows with peak = -1 (no summit) first.
summit <- peaks$start + peaks$peak
windows <- transform(peaks, start = summit - 100, end = summit + 100, peak = 100L)
windows
#>   chrom start   end strand   name score signalValue pValue qValue peak
#> 1  chr1 20050 20250      0 peak_1   500         8.1   12.3   10.2  100
#> 2  chr1 10020 10220      0 peak_2   800         9.4   15.0   12.8  100
